Fixture: 60_sawtooth_32x32_lossless.jxl
32x32 grey wrapping sawtooth, mathematically lossless, effort 3 --
OPEN BUG REPRODUCER (JPXL does not decode this correctly yet)

Purpose
-------
The "sawtooth trap" recorded in the HANDOFF ledger, promoted from a loose
description to a checked-in fixture so it stops being re-derived by hand.

  v(x, y) = (x * 7 + y * 3) mod 256

The modulo is the whole point. Where the ramp wraps, a neighbouring sample
drops by 249, so the H.5 weighted predictor sees neighbouring `true_err`
values of ~2000 sitting next to values of ~-56. That is the regime in which
the H.5.2 clamp's gating is exercised hardest, and it is where JPXL diverges.

Status at the time of writing: the stream decodes to within ONE wrong sample,
at (31, 19) -- the last column of row 19. Every sample before it matches the
source exactly; everything after is corrupted by the desynchronised entropy
stream. Full forensics, including the arithmetic showing that no reading of
H.5.2's clamp explains that sample, are in
docs/experiments/2026-08-03-h52-clamp-lower-gate-and-sawtooth.md.

-e 3 (not -e 7) is deliberate: it is what the original bug report used, and
it selects an MA tree whose leaves are both `SelfCorrecting`, so every sample
is a direct readout of the weighted prediction with nothing else able to
absorb an error.

Verification
------------
djxl decodes it to a PGM byte-identical to the source (checked on every run of
tools/make-debug-fixtures.sh), so the stream is conformant and the divergence
is JPXL's.

Modular features engaged
-------------------------
One 32x32 channel, no transforms, an MA tree of one decision node on property
15 (`max_error > 0`) with two `SelfCorrecting` leaves -- confirmed by JPXL's
own header and tree parse, both of which are believed correct (the first 639
samples decode bit-exactly).

cjxl is used strictly as a BLACK BOX: it emits conformant streams for JPXL to
parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a different libjxl
revision changes these digests, that is the point of recording them -- do not
silently update them; note the revision change.
